findings.title: White House national cyber director leaving his post
findings.summary_md: CBS News reported that multiple sources said Sean Cairncross was fired and that chief of staff Stephen Miller had long wanted him out, questioning his expertise for the national cyber director role. The report said Miller selected Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies as acting replacement and that a permanent appointment would need Senate confirmation before Democrats take control in January. It also quoted Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin saying investigators had seen nothing linking the recent Microsoft, aviation, banking and NSA outages and that he was 98 percent confident they were not malicious foreign activity.

findings.title: Kirsten A. Davies to Lead National Cyber Director Office: Axios
findings.summary_md: Bloomberg Law reported that Kirsten A. Davies had been appointed to lead the Office of the National Cyber Director, attributing the account to an Axios reporter's post on X and noting that the post cited no sources. The brief named White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller as the person making the appointment. It carried the news as a personnel appointment without describing the circumstances of Sean Cairncross's departure.

findings.title: Head of White House cyber office Sean Cairncross stepping down
findings.summary_md: The New York Post reported that Sean Cairncross was leaving after just over a year in the job and that a White House spokesperson had confirmed the departure. It said Kirsten Davies, the chief information officer at the Department of War, would replace him in an acting capacity, and relayed Axios reporting that Cairncross did not want to serve the final two years of the term and left early to allow confirmation before Democrats take the Senate in January. The report placed the exit on the same day Michael LoSapio, Trump's pick to lead CISA, testified at his Senate confirmation hearing.

findings.title: White House national cyber director is leaving after tech outages hit companies and agencies
findings.summary_md: NBC News reported that a White House official confirmed Sean Cairncross was leaving and that a source close to the White House said Pentagon CIO Kirsten A. Davies would replace him in an acting capacity, with the role requiring Senate confirmation. The report noted Cairncross had led the Office of the National Cyber Director since August 2025 and had been involved in White House AI policy deliberations. It said officials and Democratic members of Congress saw no indication the recent private and public sector outages were cyberattacks, though some suggested AI may have played a role.

findings.title: Cairncross departs abruptly after widespread tech outages
findings.summary_md: Semafor reported that Sean Cairncross was out and Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies was replacing him, citing multiple officials. One White House official and a person familiar with the White House said he was fired, with the official saying finding a new cyber director was one of Stephen Miller's first moves as chief of staff, while a senior White House official and another person familiar strongly disputed that and said he resigned without being asked. A source who said he was fired told Semafor the past week showed the need for someone more competent with the expertise to execute the role.

findings.title: The U.S. national cyber director is stepping down
findings.summary_md: TechCrunch reported that Sean Cairncross was stepping down, attributing the initial report to Axios and noting the split was described as amicable and timed to allow a Senate confirmation before Democrats take Congress in January. It said Cairncross took office in August 2025, was confirmed 59 to 35, and had no cybersecurity background before the job. The report noted the Office of the National Cyber Director was created in early 2021, that Cairncross was its third Senate-confirmed director, and that the role sat vacant for about 10 months after Chris Inglis left.

findings.title: White House removes cyber-security chief after series of tech outages
findings.summary_md: The BBC reported that the top US cybersecurity official was leaving after just over a year, citing US media reports that Cairncross had been fired after losing the confidence of Stephen Miller. It said there had been no official confirmation of the removal, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio posted that Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies was the new national cyber director. The report noted Rubio's earlier statement that there was zero evidence the outages were connected and that the US was not under systemic attack, alongside congressional scrutiny of the blackouts.
